scenes.title: An object built from thin layers
The printer deposits and cools a layer
From digital model to solid object

vo.text: A 3D printer builds a solid object by depositing material one thin layer at a time.
vo.speak: A 3D printer builds a solid object by depositing material one thin layer at a time.

vo.text: First, slicing software divides a digital 3D model into a stack of printable layers.
vo.speak: First, slicing software divides a digital 3D model into a stack of printable layers.

vo.text: For each layer, the slicer calculates the nozzle's path around the outer walls and through the inner structure.
vo.speak: For each layer, the slicer calculates the nozzle's path around the outer walls and through the inner structure.

vo.text: The printer heats the nozzle until the plastic filament can flow through its tip.
vo.speak: The printer heats the nozzle until the plastic filament can flow through its tip.

vo.text: Motors drive the nozzle along the calculated path while it extrudes a thin bead of melted plastic.
vo.speak: Motors drive the nozzle along the calculated path while it extrudes a thin bead of melted plastic.

vo.text: The deposited plastic cools and solidifies, forming the current layer of your object.
vo.speak: The deposited plastic cools and solidifies, forming the current layer of your object.

vo.text: The nozzle then rises by one layer height, or the bed lowers, and the printer repeats the process.
vo.speak: The nozzle then rises by one layer height, or the bed lowers, and the printer repeats the process.

vo.text: Each new layer fuses with the previous one, gradually building a solid shape.
vo.speak: Each new layer fuses with the previous one, gradually building a solid shape.

vo.text: So a 3D printer turns a digital model into an object through repeated extrusion, cooling, and layer bonding.
